Both the dashboard and the alert rule now exist in Kibana.

**Data exploration.** The data view `kibana_sample_data_logs` (ID `90943e30-9a47-11e8-b64d-95841ca0b247`) has a `timestamp` time field and these fields of interest:
- `response` / `response.keyword`: HTTP status code, stored as a string. The 5xx filter uses this.
- `bytes`, `clientip`, `request`, `url`, `extension`, `geo.dest`, `machine.os`, `agent`, `host`, `tags`.

I could not query the data itself. The direct Elasticsearch port is closed, and Kibana's console proxy, internal search, and ES|QL endpoints all return 400 or 404 in this instance. So the field list is the only exploration I could do, and I did not check the actual counts or time range.

**Dashboard: `EFF-0faf501a Web logs overview`** (ID `df1fa70c-70f0-4e5d-88bb-c3bfafde2a40`), default time range last 7 days, six panels:
- Total requests (ES|QL count)
- 5xx responses (ES|QL count where `response.keyword` matches `5*`)
- Average bytes per request
- Unique client IPs
- Requests over time (line)
- Requests by response code (bar)

The dashboard saved and reads back with all six panels. I have not confirmed that each ES|QL panel renders data, because I can't run queries here.

**Alert rule: `EFF-0faf501a 5xx spike`** (ID `b2bc20cf-0b06-42f3-b5be-44527fd7bd58`):
- Type: Elasticsearch query (DSL), `count` of documents where `response.keyword` matches `5*`, over `kibana_sample_data_logs`.
- Checks every 1 minute, over a 5-minute window on `@timestamp`.
- Fires when the count is greater than 10.
- Enabled, with no actions attached. It has run once and reports status `ok`.

I chose the DSL form over ES|QL because the DSL `count` maps directly onto "more than 10 requests in 5 minutes". The rule has no notification action, so it will evaluate and record alerts but will not notify anyone. Add a connector action if you want notifications.

Since the sample data is historical, the rule is unlikely to fire unless the index receives new 5xx traffic in the window.
